jobs.title: Director, Intelligent Enterprise Transformation Leader - Finance
jobs.description:
We are the leading provider of professional services to the middle market globally, our purpose is to instill confidence in a world of change, empowering our clients and people to realize their full potential. Our exceptional people are the key to our unrivaled, inclusive culture and talent experience and our ability to be compelling to our clients. You’ll find an environment that inspires and empowers you to thrive both personally and professionally. There’s no one like you and that’s why there’s nowhere like RSM.

RSM Consulting is seeking a Director to serve as Business Transformation Lead on large, integrated Intelligent Finance transformations. Our Intelligent Finance portfolio helps clients build the intelligent foundation and activate AI for Finance at scale — spanning ERP Modernization, Finance Operating Model Transformations, Finance Data & Analytics Modernization and AI Readiness, AI Enablement & Agentic Automation for the Office of Finance as well as Finance Service Delivery Transformations – including centralization, Finance Shared Services and Global Finance Service Delivery.

This is the pivotal business-side leadership role on the transformation. You own how the client operates differently once the platform is live. You are not the program manager and you are not the solution architect — you are the leader accountable for the future-state operating model, the end-to-end processes, the human experience of the change, and the executive confidence that the business, not just the technology, actually changed. Your success is measured by a single question: did the business change successfully?

You will be dedicated to one major transformation at a time, working as a peer alongside the Executive Transformation Partner, the Transformation Director, and the Platform & Delivery Lead.

Responsibilities

Operating Model and Process Ownership
Own the design and operationalization of the future-state operating model for the Finance and Operations functions — finance, supply chain, service, IT, and the shared data and reporting layer that the modernized core creates.
Lead end-to-end business capability and process design across core cycles affected by ERP, Finance point solutions, cloud, data, and AI enablement work, and define how those processes operate in a modernized, increasingly automated environment.
Define the organization, role, skill, decision-rights, and control implications of a modern core and an agentic operating environment — including which decisions become automated, which remain human, and how exceptions are handled and governed.
Establish how data ownership, stewardship, and definitional consistency are carried by the business after the build team leaves.
Maintain traceability from the client’s business case through operating-model changes, process changes, backlog priorities, adoption outcomes, and value delivered.

Human-Centered Design

Own Human-Centered Design as a funded, staffed, and measured workstream from mobilization — not a go-live activity.
Start from user jobs-to-be-done for Finance, rather than screens; ensure personas and journey maps for finance, operations, and service users drive requirements before build.
Prototype and test with real users ahead of build, and use “art-of-the-possible” demonstrations of modern and AI-enabled capability to build executive and user confidence early.
Ensure HCD findings materially shape scope — including where an AI or automation use case is not yet appropriate for the client’s data maturity or risk tolerance.

Organizational Change Management and Adoption

Own OCM as a funded, measured workstream: leader alignment and visible sponsorship from day one, stakeholder analysis, communications, resistance management, role-based training, and readiness scoring.
Baseline adoption targets and tie them explicitly to benefits realization — system usage, process compliance, automation acceptance rates, exception volumes, and reporting adoption.
Lead the business through the behavioral shift that modernization demands: fewer manual reconciliations, more trust in a single data source, and confident supervision of automated and agent-assisted work.

Backlog, Value Mapping and Delivery Cadence

Lead weekly backlog refinement and own product backlog integrity and value mapping — from business drivers through requirements, capabilities, features, adoption outcomes, and measurable benefits.
Participate in each sprint’s feature review and system demonstration alongside the client Product Owner and the Platform & Delivery Lead, assessing whether what was built changes how the business actually works.
Participate in increment planning and Inspect & Adapt retrospectives, testing outcomes against the client’s original drivers.
Ensure outcome milestones are tracked alongside technical and delivery milestones.

Transformation Leadership and Client Confidence

Serve as the bridge between technical delivery and executive confidence, presenting evidence of business change to sponsors, steering committees, and the Executive Risk Committee.
Escalate early, with a recommended action rather than a status — particularly on scope that risks delivering a platform without an operating-model change.
Plan for complexity: competing stakeholder demands, third-party and systems-integrator friction, legacy-process attachment, and key-person risk on both sides.
Bring in-person presence to large or sensitive transformations.

Practice and People Leadership

Contribute to the growth of RSM’s Total Consulting transformation capability, including methods, tools, and reusable intellectual property for operating-model design, HCD, and adoption measurement.
Mentor, coach, and develop managers and senior associates across HCD, process design, and change workstreams
Support pursuits, proposals, and thought leadership that position RSM as a leader in integrated, outcome-led modernization; help shape scope, approach, and change-workstream sizing before mobilization.
Support account expansion through demonstrated value, and maintain strong attention to engagement economics within your workstreams.

Basic Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree.
10+ years of consulting or advisory experience, including significant experience leading business-side transformation on large enterprise technology programs.
Demonstrated ownership of the Finance future-state operating model and end-to-end process design on ERP, cloud, data, or AI-enabled programs.
Demonstrated ownership of change and adoption as a funded workstream, including baselined adoption targets tied to benefits.
Experience operating in a fixed Agile or scaled-Agile cadence, including product backlog ownership, backlog refinement, and sprint demonstrations with an active client Product Owner.
Strong executive presence and the ability to hold candid, evidence-based conversations with C-suite sponsors.
Practical understanding of modern ERP, cloud, data, and AI platform capability — sufficient to shape requirements and challenge design, without acting as the technical architect.
Commitment to responsible AI use with a human in the loop and human accountability for all client-facing judgments and outputs.
Willingness and ability to travel as needed, generally up to 50%, with in-person presence on large programs.

Preferred Qualifications

CPA and / or Masters in Business Administration, with a focus on Accounting, Finance or Operations
Experience on transformations where an implementation was deliberately converted into a program as scope expanded across process, organization, and adoption.
Experience designing operating models for finance, supply chain, or shared-services functions in a modernized core environment.
Experience establishing AI and automation governance from a business-process and control perspective.
Change certification such as Prosci/ADKAR; design-thinking or service-design credentials; SAFe Agilist, PMI-ACP, or Scrum Master certification

Most roles at RSM follow a hybrid workstyle, which means team members are aligned to an RSM office and come together in person when it best supports clients, teams, development or relationship-building. jobs.title: DIRECTOR OF INFORMATION TECHNOLOGY
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

The organization has experienced strong and sustained growth since its founding in 2009 and currently employs nearly 350 people. As part of its strategic plan, the Group aims to accelerate its national and international development.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation.

The Mandate

In a context of sustained growth and transformation of its activities, Lacroix Medical Group is seeking a Director of Information Technology who will actively contribute to the organization's technological evolution.

Reporting directly to the President and CEO, the Director of IT plays a strategic role across the entire network. They are responsible for defining, structuring, and developing the IT function to effectively support the organization's operations, growth, and ambitions.

They provide leadership for technology strategy, infrastructure, business systems, cybersecurity, data governance, digital transformation, and artificial intelligence.

He is also responsible for the performance of his team and the organization's technology partner ecosystem. This role is for an experienced, business-oriented, and results-driven IT leader who can combine strategic vision with excellent execution. Your Key Responsibilities IT Strategy and Governance: Define and deploy the IT vision and master plan in line with the strategic, operational, and financial priorities of Groupe médical Lacroix. Advise senior management on investments, risks, and key technological choices.

Performance and Business Continuity

Ensure the performance, robustness, and high availability of the infrastructure and technology platforms essential to the network's medical and administrative activities, including ERP, CRM, DME, LIS, SaaS, and cloud environments.

Digital Transformation, Data, and Artificial Intelligence

Identify and prioritize initiatives to transform the organization through technology, data valorization, automation, and artificial intelligence. Lead major technology projects and ensure their effective integration into operations.

Cybersecurity and Risk Management

Maintain high standards in cybersecurity, information protection, redundancy, and business continuity in an environment where system availability and the protection of medical data are critical.

Leadership and Organizational Performance

Lead and develop a competent, autonomous, and accountable IT team. Establish clear objectives and performance indicators, ensure rigorous budget management, and optimize the contribution of suppliers, consultants, and technology partners.

An Executive Role Close to Operations

At Lacroix Medical Group, technology must meet the realities on the ground.

The IT Director will therefore need to maintain close contact with the various business units and network teams to understand their needs, anticipate challenges, and ensure that technological solutions contribute concretely to operational performance and service quality.

The position consequently requires excellent mobility. The successful candidate will be required to travel regularly throughout the Lacroix network in Quebec to meet with teams, support projects, and remain connected to the operational realities of the various facilities.

This on-the-ground presence is an essential component of the role and not an occasional responsibility.

The mandate expressly includes regular visits to service points.

The Ideal Candidate

We are looking for an experienced manager with a strong business acumen and excellent technological expertise, recognized for their leadership, judgment, and ability to drive organizational growth.

The Ideal Candidate Will Possess

A bachelor's degree in computer engineering, computer science, or a related field;
15 to 20 years of experience in information technology, including a minimum of 5 years in a management role;
Mastery of software architecture and project management;
A solid understanding of multi-site and cloud infrastructures;
Good knowledge of SaaS environments and major business platforms: ERP, CRM, financial systems, telephony, Microsoft 365, and others;
A thorough understanding of the issues cybersecurity, data governance and valorization, and artificial intelligence;
Proven experience in team management and development;
Recognized leadership in transformation and change management;
Ability to prioritize, make decisions, and manage effectively in a complex and evolving environment;
Excellent business acumen and the ability to communicate technological issues to senior management;
Fluency in French and English, both written and spoken;
A valid driver's license, a vehicle, and significant availability for regular travel throughout the network.

The Leader Profile We Are Looking For

Beyond technological expertise, we are looking for someone who stands out for their ability to mobilize, structure, and deliver.

A positive and committed leader with a strong sense of Accountability, the ability to build high-performing teams, manage rigorously, challenge the status quo, and transform technological challenges into concrete solutions for the business. The IT Director must be equally comfortable discussing strategy with senior management and understanding the challenges faced by teams in the field. Conditions and Compensation Lacroix Medical Group offers a competitive total compensation package including: Annual salary of $140,000 to $175,000, depending on experience and expertise; 4 weeks of vacation and 4 paid personal days; RRSP+ program with employer contribution; Cell phone allowance; Lacroix Health Credit; and an annual Lacroix gift card. This benefit can be combined with other benefits for personalized medical services.

Business travel expense account for trips outside your usual work area

Join a growing network and become a key player in the future of private medicine in Quebec.

Apply now and make a real difference.

BMO Capital Markets is a leading, full-service North American-based financial services provider, with over 2,700 professionals in 30 locations around the world, including 20 offices in North America, offering corporate, institutional and government clients access to a complete range of investment and corporate banking products and services. BMO Capital Markets is a member of BMO Financial Group (NYSE, TSX: BMO), one of the largest diversified financial services providers in North America with US$1.0 trillion total assets and approximately 54,000 employees as of January 31, 2025.

What is the opportunity?

The Data Cognition Team (DCT) is BMO Capital Markets’ AI engineering and enablement team, with nearly a decade of experience building and deploying AI solutions in complex, regulated financial services environments.

As Vice President, AI Strategy & Product Management, you will operate at the intersection of business strategy, product management, and AI. You will own the vision, strategy, roadmap, delivery, and adoption of high-value AI and data products, working closely with front-office users, senior leaders, engineers, data scientists, UX, risk, and compliance partners.

The successful candidate will bring the judgment, influence, and hands-on product leadership required to scale trusted AI and data products and capabilities in a highly regulated Capital Markets environment.

Align senior business, technology, data, and control-function stakeholders around product priorities, trade-offs, risks, and expected outcomes.

Our technology solutions are the foundations of everything we do from keeping the bank safe, managing global resources, and providing the technical tools our workers need to be successful to designing our digital architecture and ensuring our platforms provide a first-class customer experience. We reimagine client and partner experiences to deliver excellence through secure, reliable, and efficient services.

Our commitment to diversity includes a workforce that represents the clients we serve from all walks of life, backgrounds, and origins. We foster an environment where the best people want to work. We value and demand respect for others, promote individuals based on merit, and ensure opportunities for personal development are widely available to all. Ideal candidates are innovators with well-rounded backgrounds who bring their authentic selves to work and complement our culture of delivering results with pride. If you are a problem solver who seeks passion in your work, come join us. We’ll enable growth and progress together.

Position Overview:

The Application Development AI Developer is an intermediate level position responsible for participation in the establishment and implementation of new or revised application systems and programs in coordination with the Technology team. The overall objective of this role is to contribute to applications systems analysis and programming activities.

We are seeking a forward-thinking developer t to join our engineering team. In this role, you will implement cutting-edge artificial intelligence, leveraging Large Language Models (LLMs) and the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to build next-generation applications.

You will combine your growing AI expertise with a solid foundation in backend engineering, managing APIs, and optimizing database performance. If you are eager to work with modern developer tools, learn autonomous workflows, and build scalable solutions, this role is for you.

Responsibilities:

AI Integration: Build and deploy applications powered by LLMs, integrating prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), and basic agentic workflows.
Context Ecosystems: Implement Model Context Protocol (MCP) to securely connect AI models with local or remote data sources and tools.
API Development: Design, build, and maintain high-performance RESTful APIs to support application features.
Database Management: Write, optimize, and troubleshoot SQL queries, views, and schemas within Microsoft SQL Server.

Husky TechnologiesTM is an exciting company with tremendous potential. We have a great team and great expectations. If you are attracted to bold goals, believe in uncompromising honesty, support mutual respect, care about environmental responsibility, have a passion for excellence and a desire to make a positive contribution – then we want you to join the Husky TechnologiesTM team!

The Finance Director serves as a strategic business partner to the Leadership Team in support of Husky’s Global Service Business and Customer Success Management strategy. This role provides leadership for financial planning, forecasting, performance analysis, governance, and decision support to drive profitable growth, improve operational performance, and strengthen financial visibility across service revenue streams, including field service, contracts, parts, and other aftermarket offerings. The Finance Director is expected to influence strategic decisions, lead transformation initiatives, and build a high-performing finance capability that enables the business to scale effectively.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Planning & Forecasting

Lead the annual budget, quarterly forecast, and long-range planning processes for the service business.
Develop robust revenue, margin, cost, and headcount forecasts based on operational and commercial drivers.
Translate business strategies into financial plans with clear assumptions, risks, and opportunities.
Support scenario planning and sensitivity analysis for service growth, pricing, labor utilization, and investment decisions.

Performance Management & Analysis

Deliver timely and accurate monthly financial reporting and variance analysis for service revenue, gross margin, SG&A, and operating income.
Analyze business performance by region, product line, customer segment, channel, and service offering.
Monitor and explain key drivers of performance, including labor utilization, absorption, contract profitability, attach rates, response times, and service productivity.
Provide actionable insights and recommendations to improve growth, profitability, and working capital performance.

Business Partnering

Serve as the senior finance partner to service leadership, operations, commercial teams, and Customer Success leaders, providing insight and challenge on strategic priorities, business performance, and investment decisions.
Lead financial evaluation of pricing strategies, contract renewals, service program design, and capital or operating investments to support sustainable growth and margin expansion.
Provide proactive challenge and decision support to business leaders by identifying risks, opportunities, and trade-offs across growth, productivity, service delivery, and resource allocation.
Lead cross-functional evaluation of new service offerings, business models, and transformation initiatives that improve service coverage, utilization, fulfillment, cost efficiency, and customer value.
Sponsor finance and business transformation initiatives across Finance and Customer Success Management, including enhancements to processes, reporting, operating metrics, and decision frameworks that support growth, profitability, and scalability.

Management Reporting & KPI Development

Develop and enhance dashboards, reporting tools, and KPIs that improve transparency and decision-making.
Standardize definitions and reporting for critical service metrics across the organization.
Improve reporting automation and self-service analytics capabilities where possible.
Present clear financial results and business insights to senior leadership

Process Improvement & Governance

Strengthen forecasting accuracy, reporting discipline, and financial controls within the service business.
Drive continuous improvement in FP&A processes, planning models, and reporting frameworks.
Ensure alignment with corporate finance requirements, accounting policies, and internal controls
Support month-end close and planning processes in partnership with accounting and finance teams.

Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Economics, or a related field required.
CPA, CMA, CFA, or MBA preferred.
10+ years of progressive experience in FP&A, finance business partnering, commercial finance, or operational finance, including leadership responsibility.
Experience in a service, aftermarket, field service, maintenance, or contract-based business strongly preferred.
Strong financial modeling, forecasting, and business analysis skills.
Advanced proficiency in Excel and experience with ERP and planning/reporting systems.
Executive presence with strong communication, presentation, and stakeholder management skills, and the ability to influence senior leaders across functions and regions.
Proven ability to work cross-functionally in a fast-paced, performance-driven environment

Preferred Experience In a Service Business

Understanding of service revenue models such as time and materials, service contracts, preventive maintenance, subscriptions, and parts/service bundles.
Experience analyzing operational KPIs such as technician utilization, service efficiency, contract margins, backlog, renewal rates, and service attach rates.
Familiarity with pricing strategy, labor productivity, installed base analytics, and customer lifecycle economics

Core Competencies

Strategic leadership
Financial and commercial acumen
Analytical rigor
Executive business partnership
Influence and executive communication
Problem solving
Process improvement
Results orientation and a bias for action

Team Development

Build and lead a high-performing finance team with strong capability in financial analysis, strategic thinking, business partnership, and change leadership.
Lead, coach, and develop team members, including succession planning, capability building, and development of future finance leaders.

Financial Leadership

Provide consistent, timely, accurate, and decision-oriented financial reporting for the service business, with greater automation and self-service access to insights where possible

jobs.description:
Founded in 2000 by three former Royal Canadian Air Force (RCAF) CF-18 fighter pilots who identified an opportunity to improve military readiness training, Top Aces has since established itself as the world leader in contracted adversary air (ADAIR) services and joint terminal attack controller (JTAC) training.

We pride ourselves on our unblemished safety record, having flown an industry leading 130,000+ hours of operational training without accident in support of customers worldwide, including Canada, the U.S., Germany, and multiple other NATO allies and international partner nations.

Our vision is to be the most trusted provider of innovative defense training solutions, continuously elevating standards in an industry where "Experience Matters." This commitment to innovation and technology ensures we remain adaptable, training allied militaries to succeed against evolving threats.

Top Aces’ dynamic team contributes to delivering on our purpose of training the next generation of combat leaders by living our values of Service, Integrity, Excellence, and Together every day!

Join our team!

Essential Duties and Responsibilities:

The Director FP&A and Capital Investment is a key member of the company’s finance team and is responsible for supporting all financial planning and analysis activities across the International Division of Top Aces Inc. The director will be responsible for the division’s annual budget process, financial forecasting, financial strategic planning and business performance analysis activities. Additionally, the director will be responsible for supporting the effort to enhance the company’s continuous improvement initiatives aimed at improving profitability and efficiency. The director will provide project financial support, return on investment (ROI) analysis along with KPI development, measurement and analysis. The successful candidate will have demonstrable leadership competencies, strong attention to detail, and will work well under pressure in a fast-paced environment. The candidate will demonstrate a successful track record of working collaboratively in a dynamic environment and a matrix organizational structure.

Own the division’s annual budgeting and financial planning process (quarterly forecasts and strategic plan 5-year forecast) and review all associated financial plans and budgets.
Develop, lead, and manage core FP&A activities.
Lead the development of P&L, balance sheet and cash flow forecasts and partner with internal stakeholders to optimize working capital (prepayments, inventory) and cash flow generation.
Lead the development of scenario analysis, sensitivity analysis and risks & opportunities.

Oversee capex financial management and capex forecasting improvement initiatives.
Lead inventory financial management and work with key stakeholders to optimize the level of inventory.
Oversee the preparation of the International Division monthly management accounts, FP&A reports and dashboards, including presentations to SLT and the company’s Board of Directors.
Support the division’s Senior Leadership Team (SLT) to evaluate and review new business and investment opportunities, including new business pricing, client Total Cost of Ownership (TCO), Return on Investment (ROI), payback period and return on capital (RONA) analyses.
Support the executive team decision-making by providing insightful data and analysis with the objective of improving Top Aces’ profitability and efficiency.
Build and develop the skill sets of finance professionals under her/his direction.

Education and/or Work Experience Requirements:

Bachelor’s degree required with concentration in finance and/or accounting or comparable business field preferred.
CPA and/or MBA preferred
10-15 years of experience in relevant accounting, or financial leadership roles.
Significant expertise with data analysis and reporting.
Ability to handle multiple assignments on a timely basis with a high degree of accuracy.
High level of motivation and aptitude for problem solving, with a strong attention to detail.
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills as well as strategic thinking to effectively interface with external stakeholders and the division’s Senior Leadership Team.
Ability to translate financial data into strategic insights.
Able to work in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines, possessing a high sense of urgency.
Ability to perform all work in support of our Corporate Values of Excellence, Service, Integrity … Together.

Working Conditions:

May be required to travel from time to time
May be required to work overtime or longer hours when Top Aces Requires

Supervisory, Training and Advisory Responsibilities:

May be required to provide regular guidance, advice and training, as requested by the supervisor, to other employees supporting the function.

Occupational Health and Safety:

Employees are responsible for:

Working in compliance with Occupational Health and Safety acts and regulations
Following safe work practices and procedures and using safeguards and personal protective equipment
Reporting hazards (such as unsafe situations and activities) to their supervisor immediately.

Security Clearance Requirements/ CGP / ITAR:

Position requires Level II clearance with the Canadian Government and the ability to gain access to the Canadian Controlled Goods Program

By joining Top Aces, you will find:

A work environment in which service, integrity, excellence and teamwork are highly valued;
Opportunities for development and growth;
Multidisciplinary and multicultural collaboration at a local and global level;
A flexible schedule;
Attractive benefit plan.

Come share your passion with us! Here, you’ll be encouraged, empowered, and challenged to be your best self.

Equal Employment Opportunity

At Top Aces, all employees are welcome regardless of race, nationality, color, religion, sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, disability or age. The masculine form may be used in this job description solely for ease of reading but refers to men, women and gender diversity.

jobs.title: Director of Finance
jobs.description:
Springer Group of Companies is a well‑established, family‑owned real estate investment and development organization based in Kingston, Ontario. The organization manages a diverse portfolio of assets and operates with a long‑term, hands‑on ownership approach, emphasizing financial discipline, operational efficiency, and sustainable growth.

Reporting directly to ownership, the Director of Finance will oversee the full accounting function and play a key role in maintaining the financial health of the organization. This position is responsible for financial reporting, payroll, tax compliance, cash management, and team leadership, while working closely with external advisors to support ongoing operations and strategic initiatives.

Responsibilities

Oversee monthly, quarterly, and annual financial reporting across multiple entities.
Prepare and review quarterly financial statements and support year‑end accounting processes.
Maintain general ledger integrity, intercompany balances, and corporate records.
Manage corporate tax filings including T2s, T3s, T5s, and partnership returns, as well as quarterly tax installments.
Oversee HST, EHT, WSIB reporting and annual reconciliations.
Act as the primary point of contact for CRA correspondence, audits, and notices of assessment.
Oversee bi‑monthly payroll processing, including T4s, ROEs, employee remittances, and garnishments.
Manage employee onboarding and offboarding, payroll changes, benefits administration, and employee records.
Approve online payments, electronic workflows, and daily cheque runs.
Manage banking relationships, financing renewals, lender reporting, and cash management activities.
Track and administer GICs, mortgages, and other financing instruments.
Lead and delegate work across the accounting team, including daily prioritization and workload planning.
Maintain an accurate organizational chart and support team development initiatives.
Manage accounting systems and tools, including Yardi and related subscriptions.
Liaise with external partners including accountants, lawyers, auditors, banks, and property development partners.
Provide financial analysis, reporting, and ad hoc insights to ownership as required.

Skills & Qualifications

Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field.
CPA designation required.
Minimum five (5) years of progressive accounting or finance experience; real estate or multi‑entity experience is an asset.
Strong knowledge of financial reporting, payroll, and corporate tax compliance.
Experience managing multiple deadlines and working with external advisors.
Proficiency in Microsoft Office; experience with Yardi or similar systems is an asset.
Strong organizational skills and the ability to work independently in an owner‑led environment.

Benefits

Competitive base salary.
Paid time off.
Extended health, dental, and vision coverage.
Life insurance.
On‑site parking.

We are committed to creating an inclusive, accessible workplace in accordance with the Accessibility for Ontarians with Disabilities Act (AODA). Accommodations are available upon request for candidates during all aspects of the recruitment and selection process. If you require accommodation, please contact us at felicia.scaviarupi@mnp.ca to discuss your needs.

Experience something Brilliantly Different.

At MUFG Investor Services, we partner with some of the world’s most sophisticated public and private funds to help them operate with confidence and scale. We bring together fund administration, banking, and operational expertise to solve complex challenges across the alternatives space.

With over $1 trillion in assets under administration
and a global presence across 17 locations
, we combine deep industry knowledge with the strength of MUFG — one of the world’s largest financial institutions with approximately $3 trillion in assets

Here, you’ll do work that matters from day one. You’ll collaborate with smart, driven teams, build your expertise across complex fund structures, and grow your career in an environment that values curiosity, accountability, and new ideas. To learn more, visit us at www.mufg-investorservices.com.

Job Description

In this role, you will assist the Business Data Office – Client Data Team fulfilling mandate of ingesting and maintaining static data for clients, Data Migration and remediation, solution verification, testing and investment data maintenance for Fund of Funds.

Acknowledge and complete requests for data updates from stakeholders (Client Integration & Operations)

jobs.title: Head of Digital Performance
jobs.description:
About The Lacroix Medical Group

A leader in private medicine in Quebec, the Lacroix Medical Group
comprises three rapidly growing divisions:

Medical Clinics
Operating Rooms
Biomedical Laboratory

Since its founding in 2009, the Lacroix Medical Group has experienced sustained growth and now has nearly 350 employees across its various divisions. Driven by an ambitious and entrepreneurial vision, the organization continues its expansion across the province and aspires to accelerate its development in national and international markets.

OUR MISSION

To be the benchmark in private healthcare.

OUR VALUES

Passion | Respect | Integrity | Commitment | Innovation

Mandate

Reporting to the Director of Marketing, the Digital Performance Manager
plays a key role in the growth, reach, and success of the Lacroix Medical Group.

Passionate about digital marketing, data, and innovation, this individual leverages their expertise to develop high-performing strategies that generate a tangible impact on our business objectives. Their daily challenge: transforming data into opportunities, strategies into results, and ideas into measurable actions. In a dynamic environment encompassing multiple clinics, services, and business lines, the successful candidate will lead the organization's overall digital performance. They will develop, deploy, measure, and optimize digital media campaigns to increase our visibility, generate business opportunities, and maximize the return on our marketing investments. A true strategic partner to internal teams, this proactive individual will work closely with various stakeholders to understand their challenges, identify the best growth opportunities, and recommend innovative, results-oriented solutions. Thanks to her expertise, she actively contributes to the evolution of our digital maturity, the continuous improvement of our practices, and the achievement of our growth ambitions. Curious, analytical, and always on the lookout for new trends, the Digital Performance Manager enjoys experimenting, innovating, and pushing boundaries. Whether through campaign optimization, advanced data analytics, artificial intelligence, geolocation, or new approaches to digital marketing, this individual helps maintain the Lacroix Medical Group's position among the most innovative organizations in its sector. If you are performance-driven, thrive on challenges, and want to grow in an environment where your ideas will have a concrete and measurable impact, this position is for you. Your Role Take charge of the activation, management, and analysis of digital media campaigns (SEM, programmatic, and social media). Ensure the implementation of trafficking, online deployment, execution, daily bid monitoring, campaign health, and performance analysis. Manage and ensure adherence to media budgets while optimizing ROI. investments. Support internal clients, understand their needs, advise them, and recommend the best digital strategies. Ensure rigorous monitoring of conversions, data quality, and overall campaign performance. In-depth analysis of results, identify optimization opportunities, and share learnings with team members. Effectively navigate between multiple projects, brands, and priorities simultaneously. Manage and optimize Google Ads and Meta Ads campaigns to achieve established performance objectives. Utilize measurement and optimization tools such as Google Analytics 4, Google Search Console, and SEMrush. Design, maintain, and analyze performance dashboards in Looker Studio. Constantly monitor best practices in Generative Engine Optimization (GEO) and Search Engine Optimization (SEO). Participate to the development, implementation, and execution of digital strategies with the team's various experts. Identify and recommend new acquisition, conversion, and optimization opportunities to support the organization's growth.

The Ideal Candidate

Bachelor's degree in marketing, communications, or a related field.
Minimum of 6 to 8 years of experience in digital marketing and performance campaign management.
Experience in an environment encompassing multiple divisions, brands, or business lines.
Agency experience (a significant asset).
Valid Google Ads certification.
Excellent command of Google Ads, Meta Ads, Google Analytics 4, and Looker Studio.
Experience with other platforms and tools, including Google Tag Manager and TikTok Ads Manager.
Strong analytical skills and a strong results orientation.
Highly autonomous, rigorous, and organized.
Initiative and ability to thrive in a constantly evolving environment.
Ability to manage multiple priorities in a context of rapid growth.
Excellent command of both spoken and written French and English.
Strong interest in innovation, artificial intelligence, and the evolution of digital technologies.

Our Benefits

Lacroix Gift Card of $500 per year, including fast access to a doctor.
Annual Health Account of $1,100, which can reach $2,000 based on years of service. FTQ Workers' Fund with employer contribution. Annual budget dedicated to continuing education. Real opportunities for career advancement and professional development. Three weeks of vacation upon hiring. Four paid floating holidays per year. Hybrid work model. Free parking. Modern, bright, and collaborative work environment. Unlimited coffee and employee lounge. Join an ambitious, growing organization where your expertise, ideas, and passion will directly contribute to shaping the future of private healthcare. Quebec.
